lessons.title: Multiple Choice Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Living things use food to remain alive, breathe, move on their own, grow and produce living things of their own kind, and they have the ability to sense.
  • Plants make their own food and generally cannot move from one place to another; animals depend on plants and other animals for their food and can move from place to place.
  • Vertebrates are animals having a backbone, for example fish, frog, lizard, pigeon and cat. Invertebrates have no backbone, for example cockroach, honey bee, butterfly, starfish and snail.
  • There are four types of teeth: incisors for biting and cutting, canines for piercing and tearing, premolars for chewing and grinding, and molars also for chewing and grinding.
  • Bones and muscles work together: when muscles contract, they pull the bones, so the bone moves at the joint.
  • The lungs exchange oxygen between blood and air; the heart works like a pump and circulates blood all over the body.
  • Many plants produce fruits to protect the seeds. Fish have fins and a tail. Non-flowering plants have no flower; pine is a non-flowering plant.

Solved Exercises

Q: Which one is common among butterfly, bird and bat?

Options: (a) Teeth (b) Hair (c) Bones (d) Wings

Correct answer: Wings

Q: Many plants produce fruits:

Options: (a) to protect seeds. (b) to produce food for the seeds. (c) to store water for the seed germination. (d) to stop seeds from dispersal.

Correct answer: to protect seeds.

Q: Fish are vertebrate and swim in water. Which one of the following is true?

Options: (a) Have fur on the body (b) Have feathers and a tail (c) Have four legs (d) Have fins and a tail

Correct answer: Have fins and a tail

Q: Which part of a plant is absent in non- flowering plants?

Options: (a) Root (b) Shoot (c) Leaf (d) Flower

Correct answer: Flower

Q: Which one of the following is a non- flowering plant?

Options: (a) Apple (b) Rose (c) Mango (d) Pine

Correct answer: Pine

Q: Which statement is correct for all the vertebrates?

Options: (a) Have fur (b) Have more than four legs (c) Have backbone (d) Can fly in air

Correct answer: Have backbone

mcqs.q: Which one is common among butterfly, bird and bat?
mcqs.why: Butterflies, birds and bats are very different animals, but all three have wings and can fly. A butterfly has no teeth, hair or bones like the others, so wings are the common feature.

mcqs.q: Many plants produce fruits:
options: to produce food for the seeds.
to store water for the seed germination.
mcqs.why: Many plants produce fruits to protect the seeds inside them. The fruit covers the seeds and keeps them safe until they grow into new plants.

mcqs.q: Fish are vertebrate and swim in water. Which one of the following is true?
mcqs.why: Fish are vertebrates that swim in water. They have fins and a tail, which help them to swim. Fish do not have fur, feathers or four legs.

mcqs.q: Which part of a plant is absent in non- flowering plants?
mcqs.why: Non-flowering plants have roots, shoots and leaves, but they never produce flowers. The flower is the part absent in non-flowering plants.

mcqs.q: Which one of the following is a non- flowering plant?
mcqs.why: Apple, rose and mango plants produce flowers, so they are flowering plants. The pine does not produce flowers, so it is a non-flowering plant.

mcqs.q: Which statement is correct for all the vertebrates?
mcqs.why: Vertebrates are the animals that have a backbone (vertebral column). Not all vertebrates have fur or can fly, but every vertebrate has a backbone.

mcqs.q: Which one of the following is an invertebrate?
mcqs.why: Invertebrates are animals without a backbone. A butterfly has no backbone, while a fish, a frog and a cat all have backbones, so they are vertebrates.

mcqs.q: Which part of the body pumps blood all over the body?
mcqs.why: The heart works continuously like a pump throughout life. Its muscles contract and relax and it circulates blood all over the body through blood vessels.

mcqs.q: Which teeth are used for biting and cutting food?
mcqs.why: Incisors are used for biting and cutting food. Canines pierce and tear food, while premolars and molars are used for chewing and grinding food.

mcqs.q: How do plants get their food?
options: They depend on animals for food
mcqs.why: Plants make their own food, while animals depend on plants and other animals for their food. This is an important difference between plants and animals.

lessons.title: Short Answers and Constructed Response Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Living things breathe, use food, move on their own, grow, produce their own kind and can sense.
  • Vertebrates have a backbone (fish, frog, lizard, pigeon, cat); invertebrates have no backbone (cockroach, honey bee, butterfly, starfish, snail).
  • Incisors bite and cut food; canines pierce and tear food; premolars and molars chew and grind food. A tiger uses its large canines for piercing prey and a rat uses its large incisors for biting food.
  • Bones are united at the joints to form the skeleton; muscles attached to the bones pull them so we can sit, walk, run and jump.
  • Air enters the lungs through the nose and windpipe; the exchange of oxygen between blood and air takes place in the lungs.
  • The heart pumps blood continuously all over the body through blood vessels.

Solved Exercises

Q: Write any four characteristics of living things?

Ans: Four characteristics of living things are: (1) Living things use food to remain alive. (2) Living things breathe. (3) Living things can move on their own. (4) Living things grow and produce living things of their own kind. They also have the ability to sense.

Q: Compare any three differences between plants and animals?

Ans: Plants are usually green in colour, while animals are found in various colours. Plants make their own food, while animals depend on plants and other animals for their food. Generally, plants cannot move from one place to another, while animals can move from one place to another.

Q: Differentiate between vertebrates and invertebrates.

Ans: Vertebrates are the animals having a backbone (vertebral column), for example fish, frog, lizard, pigeon and cat. Invertebrates are the animals having no backbone, for example cockroach, honey bee, butterfly, starfish and snail.

Q: Name the types of teeth and write their functions.

Ans: There are four types of teeth. Incisors are used for biting and cutting food. Canines are used for piercing and tearing food. Premolars are used for chewing and grinding food. Molars are also used for chewing and grinding food.

Q: What functions do bones and muscles perform together?

Ans: Bones are united at the joints to form the skeleton, and muscles are attached to and cover the bones. When muscles contract, they pull the bones, so the bone moves at the joint. In this way bones and muscles work together and help us to move our hands, arms, feet and legs, and to sit, walk, run and jump.

Q: Describe the functions of lungs and heart.

Ans: During breathing, air enters our lungs through the nose and windpipe. The lungs keep expanding and contracting, and the exchange of oxygen between blood and air takes place in the lungs; when they expand we inhale air and when they contract air is exhaled. The heart works continuously like a pump throughout life; its muscles contract and relax and it circulates blood all over the body through blood vessels.

Q: The diagrams show a tiger skull and a rat skull. Describe the diagrams.

Ans: Diagram (in words): There are two skull diagrams. The upper, larger diagram is labelled 'Skull of Tiger' and its long, pointed front teeth are labelled 'canines'. The lower, smaller diagram is labelled 'Skull of Rat' and its front teeth are labelled 'incisors'. A tiger has large canines and a rat has large incisors.

Q: (a) What does a tiger do with its canines?

Ans: A tiger has large canines. It uses its canines for piercing the prey, because canines perform the function of piercing and tearing food.

Q: (b) What does a rat do with its incisors?

Ans: A rat has large incisors. It uses its incisors for biting food or killing prey, because incisors perform the function of biting and cutting food.

mcqs.q: Which one of the following is a characteristic of living things?
mcqs.why: Living things breathe, use food to remain alive, move on their own, grow and produce living things of their own kind, and they also have the ability to sense.

mcqs.q: Which one of the following animals is a vertebrate?
mcqs.why: Vertebrates are animals having a backbone. Fish, frog, lizard, pigeon and cat are vertebrates, while snail, starfish and honey bee have no backbone.

mcqs.why: Canines are sharp teeth used for piercing and tearing food. A tiger has large canines and uses them for piercing its prey.

mcqs.why: Muscles are attached to and cover the bones. When muscles contract, they pull the bones, so the bone moves at the joint and we can sit, walk, run and jump.

mcqs.q: The exchange of oxygen between blood and air takes place in the:
mcqs.why: During breathing, air enters our lungs through the nose and windpipe, and the exchange of oxygen between blood and air takes place in the lungs.

mcqs.q: A rat uses its large incisors for:
mcqs.why: A rat has large incisors. It uses its incisors for biting food or killing prey, because incisors perform the function of biting and cutting food.

mcqs.q: Generally, plants cannot:
options: move from one place to another
mcqs.why: Generally, plants cannot move from one place to another, while animals can move from one place to another. Plants stay in one place and make their own food.

mcqs.why: Molars are used for chewing and grinding food. Incisors bite and cut, canines pierce and tear, and premolars also chew and grind.

mcqs.q: Bones are united at the joints to form the:
mcqs.why: Bones are united at the joints to form the skeleton, and muscles are attached to and cover the bones. In this way bones and muscles work together and help us to move.

mcqs.q: A tiger uses its large canines to:
mcqs.why: A tiger has large canines. It uses its canines for piercing the prey, because canines perform the function of piercing and tearing food.

Q: How are the invertebrates useful for humans?

Ans: Invertebrates are animals without a backbone, such as the honey bee, butterfly, cockroach, starfish and snail. They are a useful part of biodiversity: the honey bee gives us honey, and insects like the butterfly help flowers in forming fruits and seeds. They also serve as food for many other animals, so they keep the balance of living things.

Q: Write the importance of biodiversity.

Ans: Biodiversity means the number of various types of living things found at a particular place. It is important because all these living things are different in their functions and structures and are essential for one another. If biodiversity is lost and living things become extinct due to destruction of habitat, change of climate, increase of temperature and shortage of water, the balance of life on Earth is disturbed.

Q: What is the importance of a flower?

Ans: Flowers are the beautiful, colourful part of a flowering plant. Fruits and seeds are formed from the flowers: when seeds are being formed within the flower, the area surrounding it ripens into fruit. In this way flowers produce seeds, and the seeds produce new plants.

Q: Project: Pumping of blood by the heart — what is made and what is observed?

Ans: Things needed: balloon, red color, jar, water, scissors, tape and straws (one blue and one pink). Steps: (i) Cut the balloon as per figure 1. (ii) Fill half of the jar with water and add a few drops of red colour (figure 2). (iii) Cover the mouth of the jar with the balloon (figure 3). (iv) Make two holes on the balloon about one inch apart; put the blue straw in one hole and the pink straw in the other (figure 4). (v) Cover the holes around the straws with tape and also cover the opening of the blue straw with tape; keep the jar in a tray (figure 5). (vi) Push the middle part between the two straws with your fingers. Observation: red liquid comes out of the pink straw, which is similar to the pumping of blood by the heart.

lessons.title: Multiple Choice Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • The environment is the sum of all living and non-living things around an organism; every living thing lives in a particular environment.
  • An ecosystem is the collection of abiotic and biotic components in an area.
  • Abiotic components are non-living, for example temperature, air, water, light and soil. Biotic components are living: producers (plants), consumers (animals) and decomposers (bacteria and fungi).
  • A food chain begins at a producer, for example Plant → Grasshopper → Rat → Owl.
  • If food resources increase, predators get more food, so the population of predators increases.
  • Cutting of forests and pollution harm the ecosystem; tree plantation is done for the conservation of the ecosystem.

Solved Exercises

Q: What is an ecosystem?

Options: (a) System of non-living things in an environment. (b) Area having a group of living and dead things. (c) System of living things in an environment. (d) The collection of abiotic and biotic components in an area.

Correct answer: The collection of abiotic and biotic components in an area.

Q: All the biotic components are:

Options: (a) animals (b) producers. (c) living things (d) non-living things.

Correct answer: living things

Q: Food chain:

Options: (a) begins at a producer. (b) begins at a consumer. (c) begins at a decomposer. (d) ends at producer.

Correct answer: begins at a producer.

Q: For the conservation of ecosystem:

Options: (a) forests are being cut. (b) roads are being built. (c) tree plantation is being done. (d) factories are being installed.

Correct answer: tree plantation is being done.

Q: Fungus is an example of:

Options: (a) producer. (b) consumer. (c) decomposer. (d) none of them.

Correct answer: decomposer.

mcqs.q: What is an ecosystem?
options: The collection of abiotic and biotic components in an area.
System of non-living things in an environment.
Area having a group of living and dead things.
System of living things in an environment.
mcqs.why: An ecosystem is the collection of abiotic (non-living) and biotic (living) components in an area. It is not only the living things or only the non-living things.

mcqs.q: All the biotic components are:
mcqs.why: Biotic components are the living components of an ecosystem, that is, all living things such as plants, animals, bacteria and fungi.

mcqs.q: Food chain:
mcqs.why: A food chain begins at a producer. Plants are producers because they make their own food; consumers eat the plants or other animals after that.

mcqs.q: For the conservation of ecosystem:
mcqs.why: For the conservation of the ecosystem, tree plantation is being done. Cutting forests, building roads and installing factories harm the ecosystem instead.

mcqs.q: Fungus is an example of:
mcqs.why: Fungus is an example of a decomposer. Decomposers such as bacteria and fungi break down dead things; producers make food and consumers eat other living things.

mcqs.q: Which one of the following is an abiotic component of an ecosystem?
mcqs.why: Abiotic components are the non-living components of an ecosystem, for example temperature, air, water, light and soil. Plants, animals and fungi are living, so they are biotic.

mcqs.q: In the food chain Plant → Grasshopper → Rat → Owl, the rat eats the:
mcqs.why: In this food chain the grasshopper eats the plant, the rat eats the grasshopper, and the owl eats the rat. Each step shows who eats whom.

mcqs.q: The producers in an ecosystem are:
mcqs.why: Biotic components are divided into producers, consumers and decomposers. Plants are the producers because they make their own food.

mcqs.q: If the food resources are increased, the population of predators will:
mcqs.why: If food resources are increased, more prey animals will be available. The predators will get more food, survive and reproduce better, so the population of predators will increase.

mcqs.q: Which human activity destroys the habitats of wildlife?
mcqs.why: Cutting of forests (deforestation) to establish cities, build roads and factories destroys the habitats of wildlife and affects the ecosystem badly.

lessons.title: Short Answers and Constructed Response Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Environment: all living and non-living things around an organism, interacting with each other.
  • Abiotic components: temperature, air, water, light and soil. Biotic components: producers (plants), consumers (animals) and decomposers (bacteria and fungi).
  • Food chain of the chapter: Plant → Grasshopper → Rat → Owl. The grasshopper eats the plant, the rat eats the grasshopper and the owl eats the rat.
  • Biodiversity means the number of various types of living things found at a particular place; where there is more biodiversity, living things compete for food and space.
  • Human activities harming the ecosystem: cutting of forests, pollution of environment and water, and unnecessary hunting of animals.
  • The female ostrich is light brown and sits on the eggs in the daytime; the black male warms them at night, so predators cannot easily see them.

Solved Exercises

Q: Define environment.

Ans: The environment can be defined as a sum of all living and non-living things around an organism. The living and non-living components of an environment interact with each other, and every living thing lives in a particular environment, for example a fish lives in water and a tiger lives in a forest.

Q: Write the names of three biotic and abiotic components of an ecosystem.

Ans: Abiotic components are the non-living components of an ecosystem, for example temperature, air and water (light and soil are also abiotic). Biotic components are the living components, which are divided into producers (plants), consumers (animals) and decomposers (bacteria and fungi); for example plants, animals and fungi are three biotic components.

Q: Draw a simple food chain.

Ans: Diagram (in words): The book's food chain figure shows four pictures joined by arrows in a line, with labels under them: 'Plant' → 'Grasshopper' → 'Rat' → 'Owl', and the whole figure is captioned 'Food chain'. The grasshopper eats the plant, the rat eats the grasshopper, and the owl eats the rat.

Q: If the food resources are increased what will be the effect on the population of predator?

Ans: If food resources are increased, more prey animals will be available to eat. The predators will get more food, so they will survive and reproduce better, and the population of predators will increase.

Q: Write two human activities which are affecting the ecosystem.

Ans: Two human activities affecting the ecosystem are: (1) cutting of forests (deforestation) to establish cities, build roads and factories, which destroys the habitats of wildlife; and (2) pollution of the environment and water resources, along with unnecessary hunting of animals, due to which many wild organisms have become extinct and many others have become endangered.

Q: What is the relationship between biodiversity and competition among living things in a balanced ecosystem?

Ans: Biodiversity means many types of living things live at a place. All the organisms in an ecosystem depend on the resources available in that area, but an area can provide food and place only to a limited number of living things. So where there is more biodiversity, the living things compete with each other for food and space, for example in a grassland all the herbivores compete for grass. In a balanced ecosystem this competition stays within limits and the ecosystem remains self-sustaining and durable.

mcqs.q: The environment can be defined as:
options: the sum of all living and non-living things around an organism
mcqs.why: The environment is the sum of all living and non-living things around an organism, and the living and non-living components of an environment interact with each other.

mcqs.q: Which one of the following is a decomposer?
mcqs.why: Decomposers are bacteria and fungi. Plants are producers and animals like the rat and the owl are consumers in the ecosystem.

mcqs.q: A fish lives in water and a tiger lives in a forest. This shows that:
options: every living thing lives in a particular environment
the environment has no living things
only big animals need an environment
mcqs.why: Every living thing lives in a particular environment, for example a fish lives in water and a tiger lives in a forest.

mcqs.q: In a balanced ecosystem, living things compete with each other for:
mcqs.why: An area can provide food and place only to a limited number of living things, so where there is more biodiversity, the living things compete with each other for food and space.

mcqs.q: The female ostrich sits on the eggs in the daytime because:
options: her light brown colour matches the dry ground and sand
mcqs.why: The female ostrich is light brown in colour, which matches the colour of the dry ground and sand in the daytime, so predators cannot easily see her while she warms the eggs.

mcqs.q: The male ostrich warms the eggs at night because:
options: he is black and matches the darkness of the night
mcqs.why: The male ostrich is black in colour, which matches the darkness of the night. So at night predators cannot easily see him while he sits on the eggs to warm them.

mcqs.q: Ostriches escape from predators by:
options: running at a speed of 70 kilometres per hour or fighting with their strong paw
mcqs.why: Ostriches are the largest and heaviest birds but they cannot fly. To escape from predators, they fight with their strong paw or run away with a speed of 70 kilometres per hour.

mcqs.q: Biodiversity means:
options: only one type of living thing at a place
the number of various types of living things found at a particular place
only plants found at a place
the non-living things at a place
mcqs.why: Biodiversity means the number of various types of living things found at a particular place. All these living things are different in their functions and structures and are essential for one another.

mcqs.q: Which activity has made many wild organisms endangered?
mcqs.why: Pollution of the environment and unnecessary hunting of animals are human activities due to which many wild organisms have become extinct and many others have become endangered.

mcqs.q: In the food chain Plant → Grasshopper → Rat → Owl, the owl is a:
mcqs.why: The owl eats the rat, so it is a consumer. Consumers are the animals that eat plants or other animals; plants are producers and bacteria and fungi are decomposers.

Q: The ostrich are the largest and heaviest birds but they cannot fly. To escape from the predator, they fight with their strong paw or run away with a speed of 70 kilometer per hour. The light brown coloured female lays eggs. The female sits on eggs at the day time, whereas the black coloured male warm them at night. (a) Why female warms eggs at day time?

Ans: The female ostrich is light brown in colour, which matches the colour of the dry ground and sand in the day time. So in daylight the predators cannot easily see her while she sits on the eggs to warm them, and the eggs remain safe.

Q: (b) Why male warms eggs at night?

Ans: The male ostrich is black in colour, which matches the darkness of the night. So at night the predators cannot easily see him while he sits on the eggs to warm them, and the eggs remain safe from predators.

Q: Project: Make a model of ecosystem using abiotic and biotic components of ecosystem — what is made and what is observed?

Ans: A model of an ecosystem is made from at least two bottles. (i) Cut the bottles as shown in the picture. In the first bottle pour water to show the aquatic ecosystem; in the second bottle put soil and a small plant to show the land ecosystem. (ii) Connect the ecosystems of both bottles (connect soil with water with a thick thread) so that the plant may receive water and minerals. The model's figure is labelled 'Plant', 'Soil', 'Thick thread' and 'Water', and the cut line on the bottle is labelled 'Cut'. (iii) Observe it daily and write a report of the result: the plant receives water and minerals through the thick thread and keeps growing, showing how abiotic and biotic components work together in an ecosystem.

lessons.title: Multiple Choice Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Three reasons of sickness are germs, shortage of healthy food and pollution.
  • A disease which can be transmitted from one person to another is a contagious disease, for example flu, polio, Tuberculosis (TB), hepatitis and COVID-19. Diabetes and cancer are non-contagious diseases.
  • Polio is caused by a virus. Milk contains the most calcium among the given foods.
  • For prevention from contagious diseases it is necessary to wear a mask, wash hands and get vaccinated.
  • In vaccination, weak or dead germs are injected into the body; antibodies are produced in the blood and immunity develops.
  • A balanced diet contains different kinds of food in proper quantities from all four groups: dairy, grain, meat/protein, and fruit and vegetable.

Solved Exercises

Q: If our body temperature increases from 98.6°F to 101°F then it's cause is:

Options: (a) hot weather (b) fever (c) sitting in the sun (d) sitting near fire

Correct answer: fever

Q: In which food most of the calcium is found?

Options: (a) Meat (b) Rice (c) Milk (d) Pulse

Correct answer: Milk

Q: If you have flu then what you will do to save yourself and others?

Options: (a) will exercise (b) will sleep for more time (c) will sit in the sun (d) will wear mask

Correct answer: will wear mask

Q: What is the cause of polio?

Options: (a) Bacteria (b) Virus (c) House fly (d) Mosquito

Correct answer: Virus

Q: It is necessary for the prevention from contagious disease:

Options: (a) Wearing mask, washing hand, vaccination. (b) Wearing mask, washing hand sitting in the sun. (c) Washing hands, sitting in the sun, sleeping more. (d) Vaccination, washing hand, not sitting in the sun.

Correct answer: Wearing mask, washing hand, vaccination.

mcqs.why: The normal body temperature is 98.6°F. If our body temperature increases from 98.6°F to 101°F, its cause is fever, not hot weather or sitting in the sun or near fire.

mcqs.q: In which food most of the calcium is found?
mcqs.why: Milk contains the most calcium among the given foods. Milk is in the dairy group of food, which is rich in calcium that makes our bones and teeth strong.

mcqs.q: If you have flu then what you will do to save yourself and others?
mcqs.why: Flu is a contagious disease that spreads from one person to another. If you have flu, you will wear a mask to save yourself and others from the germs.

mcqs.q: What is the cause of polio?
mcqs.why: Polio is a contagious disease caused by a virus. Bacteria, house flies and mosquitoes are not the cause of polio itself.

mcqs.q: It is necessary for the prevention from contagious disease:
options: Wearing mask, washing hand sitting in the sun.
Washing hands, sitting in the sun, sleeping more.
Vaccination, washing hand, not sitting in the sun.
mcqs.why: For the prevention from contagious diseases it is necessary to wear a mask, wash hands and get vaccination. Sitting in the sun or sleeping more does not prevent contagious diseases.

mcqs.q: Which one of the following is a contagious disease?
mcqs.why: A disease which can be transmitted from one person to another is called a contagious disease, for example flu, polio, Tuberculosis (TB), hepatitis and COVID-19. Diabetes and cancer are non-contagious.

mcqs.q: In vaccination, what is injected into the body?
options: Weak or dead germs of a disease
mcqs.why: In the vaccination process, the weak or dead germs of a disease are injected into the body. Antibodies are then produced in the blood to fight the disease and immunity develops.

mcqs.q: A balanced diet contains food from:
options: all four food groups in proper quantities
mcqs.why: A balanced diet contains different kinds of food in proper quantities and proportions from all four groups: dairy group, grain group, meat/protein group and fruit and vegetable group.

mcqs.q: Which one of the following is NOT a reason of sickness?
mcqs.why: Three reasons of sickness are germs, shortage of healthy food and pollution. By taking a balanced diet we remain healthy and energetic, so it is not a reason of sickness.

mcqs.q: The normal temperature of our body is:
mcqs.why: The normal body temperature is 98.6°F. When it increases to 101°F, it is fever, which is a sign of sickness in the body.

lessons.title: Short Answers and Constructed Response Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Coughing is an instant response of the body that removes the obstruction of the windpipe, such as mucus.
  • Filtration separates the particles present in water through a filter, but it does not kill germs.
  • Germs in water are killed by boiling the water for 5 to 10 minutes; chlorine is used for this purpose in large filtration plants.
  • Water can be made suitable for drinking by boiling and by filtration.
  • Healthy life: take a balanced diet, drink clean water, exercise regularly, brush teeth twice a day, wash hands with soap for at least 20 seconds, and sleep 8 to 10 hours daily (children).
  • If the body temperature rises from 98.6°F to 101°F, the cause is fever; if you have flu, wear a mask to save yourself and others.

Solved Exercises

Q: Write any three reasons of sickness.

Ans: Three reasons of sickness given in the chapter are germs, shortage of healthy food and pollution. Germs cause many diseases, and we fall ill when we do not get proper healthy food. Pollution also makes people sick.

Q: Differentiate between contagious and non-contagious diseases.

Ans: A disease which can be transmitted from one person to another person is called a contagious disease, for example flu, polio, Tuberculosis (TB), hepatitis and COVID-19. A non-contagious disease is not transmitted from one person to another, for example diabetes and cancer.

Q: Write a benefit of coughing?

Ans: Cough is an instant response of our body due to the soreness and scratchiness of the throat. The benefit of coughing is that it removes the obstruction of the windpipe, such as mucus of the wind pipe.

Q: How does vaccination save us from diseases?

Ans: In the vaccination process, the weak or dead germs of a disease are injected into the body. Antibodies are then produced in the blood to fight the disease and immunity develops in the body. In this way vaccination improves the immunity of the body and saves us from diseases.

Q: What is meant by balanced diet?

Ans: A diet that contains different kinds of food in proper quantities and proportions to fulfil the need of the body is called a balanced diet. It includes food from all four groups: dairy group, grain group, meat/protein group and fruit and vegetable group. By taking a balanced diet we remain healthy and energetic.

Q: Look at the picture of drinking water filtration plant for the public and write the answers. i. What is the function of filter?

Ans: The function of a filter is to clean water by separating the particles present in it. When water is passed through the filter, the particles present in water cannot pass through the pores of the filter and we get clean water. This process is called filtration.

Q: Can filtration also stops the germs?

Ans: No. Filtration only separates the particles present in water; it does not kill the germs. That is why chlorine is used in large filtration plants to kill the germs, and at home germs are killed by boiling the water.

Q: How can germs be killed in water?

Ans: Germs in water can be killed by boiling. Keep on heating water in a pot till boiling, then let it boil for another 5 to 10 minutes; due to this the germs present in water will be killed. Chlorine is also used for this purpose in large filtration plants.

Q: How can water be made suitable for drinking?

Ans: Water can be made clean and suitable for drinking by two methods: boiling and filtration. Boiling kills the germs present in water, and filtration separates the particles present in water through a filter, so we get clean water.

mcqs.q: The benefit of coughing is that it:
options: removes the obstruction of the windpipe
mcqs.why: Cough is an instant response of our body due to the soreness and scratchiness of the throat. Its benefit is that it removes the obstruction of the windpipe, such as mucus of the windpipe.

mcqs.q: Filtration of water separates:
mcqs.why: The function of a filter is to clean water by separating the particles present in it. The particles cannot pass through the pores of the filter, so we get clean water. This process is called filtration.

mcqs.q: Filtration alone cannot make water germ-free because it:
mcqs.why: Filtration only separates the particles present in water; it does not kill the germs. That is why chlorine is used in large filtration plants to kill the germs, and at home germs are killed by boiling.

mcqs.q: Germs in water are killed by boiling the water for:
mcqs.why: Keep on heating water in a pot till boiling, then let it boil for another 5 to 10 minutes; due to this the germs present in water will be killed.

mcqs.q: In large filtration plants, germs are killed by using:
mcqs.why: Filtration separates particles but does not kill germs, so chlorine is used in large filtration plants to kill the germs in water.

mcqs.q: Water can be made suitable for drinking by:
mcqs.why: Water can be made clean and suitable for drinking by two methods: boiling, which kills the germs, and filtration, which separates the particles present in water.

mcqs.q: For how many seconds should we wash hands properly with soap?
mcqs.why: One principle of a healthy life is to wash hands properly with soap for at least 20 seconds before and after meals and after using the toilet.

mcqs.q: Children must sleep daily for:
mcqs.why: Getting enough sleep is a principle of living a healthy life, and children must sleep 8 to 10 hours daily.

mcqs.q: Antibodies are produced in the blood after vaccination to:
options: fight the disease and develop immunity
mcqs.why: When weak or dead germs are injected in vaccination, antibodies are produced in the blood to fight the disease and immunity develops in the body, which saves us from diseases.

mcqs.q: Which one of the following is a non-contagious disease?
mcqs.why: A non-contagious disease is not transmitted from one person to another, for example diabetes and cancer. Flu, polio and hepatitis are contagious diseases.

Q: Interview a doctor or a health worker and enquire about the principles of living a healthy life. Write in the table.

Ans: The principles of living a healthy life, as given in this chapter, are: 1. Take a balanced diet with proper quantity of food from all food groups. 2. Drink clean water. 3. Exercise regularly, for example walking, running and playing. 4. Brush your teeth twice a day, once in the morning after getting up and at night before going to sleep, and wash hands properly with soap for at least 20 seconds before and after meals and after using the toilet. 5. lessons.title: Multiple Choice Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Anything which occupies space and possesses mass is called matter. Matter occurs in three states: solid, liquid and gas.
  • Solids have a definite shape and volume; liquids have a definite volume but no definite shape; gases have no definite shape and volume.
  • Gas has the lowest density because its particles are much farther apart from one another than in a solid or a liquid.
  • Metal is a better conductor of heat than wood, so cooking utensils are made of metals like iron, copper and aluminium.
  • Rubber is a non-conductor; it does not allow electricity to pass through it, so rubber gloves protect an electrician from electric shock.
  • Ice floats on the surface of water, partly above it. The order of water, ice and steam from coldest to hottest is: ice, water, steam.

Solved Exercises

Q: Which one of these has the most volume?

Options: (a) Book (b) Pencil (c) Eraser (d) Cricketbat

Correct answer: Cricketbat

Q: Which one of these groups is the correct example of the three states of matter?

Options: (a) Snow, Rain, Cloud (b) Dew, Rain, Water vapours (c) Snow, Cloud, Steam (d) Rain, Water vapours, Cloud

Correct answer: Snow, Rain, Cloud

Q: Put two spoons made of steel and wood in a cup of hot water. After few minutes the steel spoon become hot whereas, the wooden spoon does not become hot. What does it show?

Options: (a) The steel became hot soon in the presence of wood. (b) Metal is a better conductor of heat than wood. (c) Wood is a better conductor of heat than metal. (d) Metal heats the water quickly than wood.

Correct answer: Metal is a better conductor of heat than wood.

Q: A piece of ice has been put into a glass of water. Which picture is showing the correct position of the ice?

Options: (a) A - ice sunk to the bottom of the glass (b) B - ice sunk in the middle of the water (c) C - ice in the upper middle of the water, fully under the surface (d) D - ice floating at the surface of the water, partly above it

Correct answer: D - ice floating at the surface of the water, partly above it

Q: Water, ice and steam all have different temperatures. What is the order from coldest to hottest?

Options: (a) Steam, Ice, Water (b) Ice, Steam, Water (c) Steam, Water, Ice (d) Ice, Water, Steam

Correct answer: Ice, Water, Steam

mcqs.q: Which one of these has the most volume?
mcqs.why: Volume is the space occupied by a thing. Among a book, a pencil, an eraser and a cricket bat, the cricket bat is the biggest, so it has the most volume.

mcqs.q: Which one of these groups is the correct example of the three states of matter?
mcqs.why: The three states of matter are solid, liquid and gas. Snow is the solid form of water, rain is liquid water, and clouds are made of water vapour, the gas form, so this group shows all three states.

mcqs.q: Put two spoons made of steel and wood in a cup of hot water. After few minutes the steel spoon become hot whereas, the wooden spoon does not become hot. What does it show?
options: The steel became hot soon in the presence of wood.
Wood is a better conductor of heat than metal.
Metal is a better conductor of heat than wood.
Metal heats the water quickly than wood.
mcqs.why: The steel spoon became hot while the wooden spoon did not. This shows that metal is a better conductor of heat than wood, so heat passed quickly through the steel spoon.

mcqs.q: A piece of ice has been put into a glass of water. Which picture is showing the correct position of the ice?
options: A - ice sunk to the bottom of the glass
B - ice sunk in the middle of the water
C - ice in the upper middle of the water, fully under the surface
D - ice floating at the surface of the water, partly above it
mcqs.why: Ice is lighter than water, so a piece of ice floats at the surface of the water, partly above it. It does not sink to the bottom or stay fully under the surface.

mcqs.q: Water, ice and steam all have different temperatures. What is the order from coldest to hottest?
mcqs.why: Ice is the coldest, then water, and steam is the hottest. So the order from coldest to hottest is: Ice, Water, Steam.

mcqs.q: Anything which occupies space and possesses mass is called:
mcqs.why: Anything which occupies space and possesses mass is called matter. Matter generally occurs in three states: solid, liquid and gas, for example a brick is a solid and water is a liquid.

mcqs.q: Which state of matter has a definite shape and volume?
mcqs.why: Solids have a definite shape and volume; their particles are strongly attached with each other. Liquids have a definite volume but no definite shape, and gases have neither.

mcqs.q: Which state of matter has the lowest density?
mcqs.why: Gas has the lowest density. The particles in a gas are much farther apart from one another than in a solid or a liquid, so the mass present in a definite volume is the least in a gas. (The book prints the word as 'destiny'; it means density.)

mcqs.q: Cooking utensils are made of metals because metals are:
mcqs.why: Cooking utensils are made of metals because metals are good conductors of heat, for example iron, copper and aluminium. Heat passes quickly through the metal to the food inside.

mcqs.q: Which one of the following is a liquid?
mcqs.why: Water is a liquid: it has a definite volume but no definite shape and takes the shape of the vessel. A brick and a table are solids, and steam is a gas.

lessons.title: Short Answers and Constructed Response Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • In a solid, particles are strongly attached, have strong forces of attraction and vibrate about their mean position. In a gas, particles are far apart, move fast and can move freely in all directions.
  • Liquids take the shape of the vessel in which they are poured, but their volume remains the same.
  • Metals are shiny; some are hard and strong (iron) and some are soft (gold, silver, copper). Metals are used for bells because they give a clear ringing sound, and for ornaments because they are shiny.
  • Copper and aluminium allow electricity to pass and are used for electric wires; wood and rubber are non-conductors.
  • A cricket bat has more volume than a book, a pencil or an eraser.

Solved Exercises

Q: Define matter and write the name of its three states.

Ans: Anything which occupies space and possesses mass is called matter. Matter generally occurs in three states: solid, liquid and gas. For example, a brick is a solid, water is a liquid and the steam rising from boiling water is a gas.

Q: Differentiate between solid and liquid.

Ans: Solids have a definite shape and volume; their particles are strongly attached with each other and they cannot be easily pressed, for example book, table, pen and chair. Liquids have a definite volume but no definite shape; they take the shape of the vessel in which they are poured, for example water poured from a cup into a glass changes its shape but its volume remains the same.

Q: Which state of matter has lowest destiny?

Ans: Gas has the lowest density. The particles in a gas are much farther apart from one another than in a solid or a liquid, so the mass present in a definite volume is the least in a gas. (The book prints this word as 'destiny'; it means density.)

Q: Compare the arrangement of particles in solid and gas.

Ans: In a solid, the particles are strongly attached with each other, have strong forces of attraction, and vibrate to and fro about their mean position, so solids maintain a definite shape and volume. In a gas, the particles are much farther apart from one another, move fast because of weaker forces of attraction, and can move freely in all directions and occupy all the available space, so gases have no definite shape and volume.

Q: Why are the cooking utensils made of metals?

Ans: Cooking utensils are made of metals because metals are good conductors of heat, for example iron, copper and aluminium. Heat passes quickly through the metal to the food inside, so the food cooks properly. Metals are also usually hard and strong, so the utensils do not break easily.

Q: Why does the electrician wear rubber gloves during repairing of electric switch at your home?

Ans: Rubber is a non-conductor: it does not allow electricity (and heat) to pass through it, like wood and rubber given in the chapter as non-conductors. Metals such as copper and aluminium allow electricity to pass and are used for electric wires, but rubber gloves stop the electricity from reaching the electrician's hands. So the gloves protect him from an electric shock while repairing the switch.

mcqs.q: In a solid, the particles:
options: are far apart and move freely
are strongly attached and vibrate about their mean position
mcqs.why: In a solid, the particles are strongly attached with each other, have strong forces of attraction, and vibrate to and fro about their mean position, so solids maintain a definite shape and volume.

mcqs.q: When water is poured from a cup into a glass, its shape changes but its volume:
mcqs.why: Liquids have a definite volume but no definite shape; they take the shape of the vessel in which they are poured. Water poured from a cup into a glass changes its shape but its volume remains the same.

mcqs.q: In a gas, the particles move fast because:
options: the forces of attraction are strong
the forces of attraction are weaker
mcqs.why: In a gas, the particles are much farther apart from one another, move fast because of weaker forces of attraction, and can move freely in all directions and occupy all the available space.

mcqs.q: An electrician wears rubber gloves while repairing a switch because rubber:
options: is a good conductor of electricity
does not allow electricity to pass through it
mcqs.why: Rubber is a non-conductor: it does not allow electricity to pass through it. The gloves stop the electricity from reaching the electrician's hands and protect him from an electric shock.

mcqs.q: Metal is used in a bell because:
options: metals give a clear ringing sound and do not break easily
mcqs.why: Metal is used in the bell because metals usually have more density and give a clear ringing sound when struck. Metals are also hard and strong, so a metal bell does not break.

mcqs.q: Metals are preferred for making ornaments because all metals are:
mcqs.why: Metals are preferred for making ornaments because all the metals are shiny, which makes the ornaments look beautiful. Soft metals like gold, silver and copper can easily be shaped into ornaments.

mcqs.q: Which metals are used for electric wires?
mcqs.why: Metals such as copper and aluminium allow electricity to pass through them and are used for electric wires, while rubber and wood are non-conductors.

mcqs.q: Which metal is hard and strong and used to make tools and machines?
mcqs.why: Iron is a shiny, hard and strong metal of grey colour. It is used to make tools, machines and cooking utensils. Gold, silver and copper are soft metals.

mcqs.q: Aluminium is used as foil to cover cooked food because it is:
mcqs.why: Aluminium is a shiny, light metal used for utensils and wire and as foil to cover cooked food. Most metals are grey, while aluminium is light blue in colour.

mcqs.q: Which one of the following is a non-conductor?
mcqs.why: Wood and rubber are given in the chapter as non-conductors: they do not allow electricity and heat to pass through them easily. Copper, aluminium and iron are metals and conductors.

Q: Why is metal used in the bell?

Ans: Metal is used in the bell because metals usually have more density, and if you strike any metal you can hear the sound of the metal due to its density. Metals are also hard and strong, so a metal bell gives a clear ringing sound and does not break.

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Forms of Energy and Energy Transfer

lessons.title: Multiple Choice Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Light, heat, sound and electrical energy are forms of energy; water is not a form of energy.
  • Sound is produced by vibrations and needs a medium to travel, so sound cannot travel through space. Light and heat can travel through space without a medium.
  • We hear an echo when sound comes back after bouncing off a wall at a certain distance.
  • Sunlight has seven colours: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet. A rainbow is seen after rain when sunlight passes through water droplets.
  • In a television, electrical energy is transformed into light energy and sound energy. Electrical energy can also be transformed into heat.
  • Heat always travels from a hot object to a cold object. If a hand is taken nearer to the lighted lamp than to the wall, its shadow will be bigger.

Solved Exercises

Q: Which of the following is NOT a form of energy?

Options: (a) Light (b) Sound (c) Water (d) Heat

Correct answer: Water

Q: We hear echo when sound:

Options: (a) reaches us direct from the source. (b) comes after bouncing back from a wall at a certain distance. (c) comes from a loud speaker. (d) is very loud.

Correct answer: comes after bouncing back from a wall at a certain distance.

Q: How many colours are present in sunlight?

Options: (a) 1 (b) 3 (c) 5 (d) 7

Correct answer: 7

Q: If you take your hand nearer to the lighted lamp than to the wall, the shadow of your hand:

Options: (a) will not form. (b) will be smaller. (c) will be bigger. (d) will be of the same size.

Correct answer: will be bigger.

Q: Electrical energy can be transformed into:

Options: (a) heat. (b) light. (c) sound. (d) all of these.

Correct answer: all of these.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a form of energy?
mcqs.why: Light, sound and heat are forms of energy. Water is a form of matter, not a form of energy, so water is the one that is NOT a form of energy.

mcqs.q: We hear echo when sound:
options: reaches us direct from the source.
comes after bouncing back from a wall at a certain distance.
mcqs.why: We hear an echo when sound comes after bouncing back from a wall at a certain distance. The sound that reaches us direct from the source is not an echo.

mcqs.q: How many colours are present in sunlight?
mcqs.why: Sunlight is made of seven colours: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet. These seven colours are also seen in a rainbow.

mcqs.q: If you take your hand nearer to the lighted lamp than to the wall, the shadow of your hand:
options: will be of the same size.
mcqs.why: A shadow becomes bigger when the object is nearer to the light source. If you take your hand nearer to the lighted lamp than to the wall, the shadow of your hand will be bigger.

mcqs.q: Electrical energy can be transformed into:
mcqs.why: Electrical energy can be transformed into heat (as in an iron), light (as in a bulb) and sound (as in a radio or television), so it can change into heat, light and sound.

mcqs.q: Which one of the following is a form of energy?
mcqs.why: Heat is a form of energy, like light, sound and electrical energy. Water, wood and stone are forms of matter, not energy.

mcqs.q: Sound cannot travel through space because:
options: there is no air or medium in space
mcqs.why: Sound is produced by vibrations and these vibrations reach our ears through the particles of the air, so sound needs a medium to travel. There is no air in space, so sound cannot travel there.

mcqs.q: In a television, electrical energy is transformed into:
mcqs.why: In a television, electrical energy is transformed into light energy and sound energy. The light gives us the picture on the screen and the sound lets us hear the voices and music.

mcqs.q: A rainbow is formed when sunlight passes through:
options: drops of water suspended in the air after rain
mcqs.why: After rain, some drops of water are suspended in the air, and when sunlight passes through these water droplets, they divide it into seven colours, like a prism. This band of seven colours is called a rainbow.

mcqs.q: Which energy reaches us from the Sun across space?
mcqs.why: Light and heat can travel through space. The Sun is the biggest source of energy on Earth, and its energy reaches us across space — we see it as light and feel it as heat.

lessons.title: Short Answers and Constructed Response Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • The Sun is the biggest source of energy on Earth; its light and heat reach us across space.
  • The buzzing of a mosquito is produced by the fast vibrations of its wings, which travel through the air to our ears.
  • A lighted bulb gives out heat along with light, so a thermometer brought near it shows a rise in temperature as the mercury expands.
  • A reflector is a shiny and smooth surface; it bounces light forward in one direction, so a torch with a reflector (Sidra's) throws more light on a wall than a torch without one (Ali's).
  • A simple electric circuit can be completed by joining a metal object like a nail or a key with the ends of the wire; cotton bud, plastic pen, ice-cream stick and pencil do not complete the path.

Solved Exercises

Q: Can light and heat travel through space?

Ans: Yes, light and heat can travel through space. The Sun is the biggest source of energy on Earth, and its energy reaches us across space — we see it as light and feel it as heat. Unlike sound, light and heat do not need air or any other medium to travel.

Q: Why sound cannot travel through space?

Ans: Sound is produced by vibrations in an object, and these vibrations reach our ears through the particles of the air, so sound needs a medium to travel. There is no air in space, so sound cannot travel there. That is why we cannot hear the sound of explosions in the Sun.

Q: How do we sense the buzzing of mosquito?

Ans: The buzzing of a mosquito is a sound produced by the fast vibrations of its wings. These vibrations travel through the particles of the air and reach our ears. In this way we hear and sense the buzzing of the mosquito.

Q: Into which two forms, the electrical energy is transformed in a television?

Ans: In a television, electrical energy is transformed into light energy and sound energy. The light gives us the picture on the screen and the sound lets us hear the voices and music. This is an example of electrical energy changing into other forms of energy.

Q: When can we see rainbow? How is it formed?

Ans: We can see a rainbow after rain. After rain, some drops of water are suspended in the air, and when sunlight passes through these water droplets, they divide it into seven colours — red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet — like a prism. This band of seven colours in the sky is called a rainbow.

Q: If we bring a thermometer near a lighted bulb, will the thermometer show change in temperature? If yes, would the temperature rise or fall? Explain.

Ans: Yes, the thermometer will show a change and the temperature will rise. A lighted bulb gives out heat along with light, and heat always travels from a hot object to a cold object, so heat from the bulb reaches the thermometer. When the bulb of the thermometer gets this heat, the mercury inside it expands and rises in the glass tube, showing a higher temperature.

Q: You are holding a glass of cold water in a room. The temperature of different things is as follows: Your temperature: 37 °C, Temperature of water: 5 °C, Temperature of room: 30 °C. Draw arrows in the picture to show the directions of the heat flow.

Ans: Diagram (in words): The picture shows a hand holding a cup of cold water, with the labels 5 °C on the water in the cup, 30 °C for the room and 37 °C for the hand holding the cup. Heat always travels from a hot object to a cold object, so the arrows of heat flow point towards the cold water: one arrow from the hand (37 °C, the hottest) into the water (5 °C), and one arrow from the warmer room air (30 °C) into the water (5 °C). No arrow points away from the water, because the cold water does not give heat to the hotter hand or room.

Q: Sidra has a reflector in her torch. There is no reflector in the torch of Ali. Which torch will throw more light on a wall at 5-meter distance? Tick (✓) in the right box. (Ali's torch / Sidra's torch)

Ans: Sidra's torch will throw more light on the wall. The reflector in her torch is a shiny and smooth surface, so the light striking it bounces back and is sent forward in one direction, as in reflection of light. Ali's torch has no reflector, so its light spreads out and less light reaches the wall 5 metres away.

mcqs.q: The buzzing of a mosquito is produced by:
options: the fast vibrations of its wings
its body striking the air once
mcqs.why: The buzzing of a mosquito is a sound produced by the fast vibrations of its wings. These vibrations travel through the particles of the air and reach our ears.

mcqs.q: If we bring a thermometer near a lighted bulb, the temperature shown will:
mcqs.why: A lighted bulb gives out heat along with light, and heat travels from a hot object to a cold object. The mercury in the thermometer expands with this heat and rises, showing a higher temperature.

mcqs.q: Heat always travels:
options: from a cold object to a hot object
from a hot object to a cold object
mcqs.why: Heat always travels from a hot object to a cold object. That is why heat from a hand at 37 °C and from room air at 30 °C flows into cold water at 5 °C, and not away from it.

mcqs.q: Sidra's torch has a reflector and Ali's torch has none. Which torch will throw more light on a wall 5 metres away?
mcqs.why: The reflector in Sidra's torch is a shiny and smooth surface, so the light striking it bounces back and is sent forward in one direction. Ali's torch has no reflector, so its light spreads out and less light reaches the wall.

mcqs.q: To complete a broken electric circuit so that the bulb lights up, we should join the ends of the wire with:
mcqs.why: Metal lets the electric current pass through it, so joining a metal object — the nail or the key — with the ends of the wire completes the electric path and the bulb lights up. The cotton bud, plastic pen, ice-cream stick and pencil are not metals.

mcqs.q: We cannot hear the sound of explosions in the Sun because:
options: the Sun is too far for light
mcqs.why: Sound needs a medium like air to travel, and there is no air in space. That is why we cannot hear the sound of explosions in the Sun, although its light and heat reach us.

mcqs.q: The seven colours of sunlight are:
options: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet
red, pink, brown, black, white, grey and blue
mcqs.why: When sunlight passes through water droplets after rain, it is divided into seven colours — red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet — which form the rainbow.

mcqs.q: A reflector in a torch is:
mcqs.why: The reflector in a torch is a shiny and smooth surface, so the light striking it bounces back and is sent forward in one direction, as in the reflection of light.

mcqs.q: In the experiment with cold water (5 °C), a hand (37 °C) and a room (30 °C), the heat flows:
options: from the water to the hand and the room
towards the cold water from the hand and the room
from the room to the hand only
mcqs.why: Heat always travels from a hot object to a cold object, so the arrows of heat flow point towards the cold water: from the hand (37 °C) and from the warmer room air (30 °C) into the water (5 °C).

mcqs.q: A simple telephone made of two paper cups and a string shows that sound:
options: is produced by vibrations and travels along the string
mcqs.why: When one person speaks into one cup, the vibrations of the sound travel along the tight string and the other person hears the sound in the second cup, showing that sound is produced by vibrations and needs a medium to travel.

Q: A simple electric circuit consists of battery, bulb and electric wire. Its electric path has broken and the bulb is not glowing. We want to complete the electric path so that bulb can light up by using the electric energy of the battery. We have cotton bud, a plastic ball pen, an ice-cream stick, nail, a key and a pencil. Which thing should we join with the ends of the wire so that electric circuit is complete and the bulb lights up?

Ans: Diagram (in words): The circuit diagram shows a Bulb at the top, an Electric wire on the left side and a Battery or Cell at the bottom, with a break in the path on the right side; the objects shown below are labelled Nail, Ice-cream stick, Key, Pencil and Cotton bud (the plastic ball pen is named in the text). We should join a metal object — the nail or the key — with the ends of the wire. Metal lets the electric current pass through it, so the electric path becomes complete and the bulb lights up, while cotton bud, plastic ball pen, ice-cream stick and pencil are not metals and do not complete the path.

Q: Project: Let us make a telephone — what is made and what is observed?

Ans: A simple telephone is made from two paper cups, two small pieces of twig, a string or thin wire (7 metres) and a pencil or nail for making holes in the paper cups, as shown in the diagram labelled Paper Cup at each end and String or wire joining them. A hole is made in the bottom of each cup, the string or wire is passed through and tied with the twigs so that the two cups are joined by the tight string. When one person speaks into one cup, the vibrations of the sound travel along the string and the other person hears the sound in the second cup, showing that sound is produced by vibrations and needs a medium to travel.

lessons.title: Multiple Choice Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Force is a push or a pull. When a body changes its position, it is called motion.
  • All bodies are attracted towards the Earth due to gravity. Gravity acts on all objects.
  • Friction is the force that stops or tends to stop moving objects; it always acts against the direction of movement.
  • With the same force, a toy car travels longer on a smooth marble floor than on rocky soil, brick floor or ground, because there is less friction.
  • A pulley is a simple machine that consists of a grooved wheel with a rope. Other simple machines are the lever, gear and ramp (inclined plane).

Solved Exercises

Q: What is force?

Options: (a) Push (b) Pull (c) Lift (d) Push and pull

Correct answer: Push and pull

Q: When a body changes its position, it is called:

Options: (a) friction (b) force (c) motion (d) gravity

Correct answer: motion

Q: All bodies are attracted towards the Earth due to:

Options: (a) force (b) friction (c) gravity (d) motion

Correct answer: gravity

Q: If we apply the same force on a toy car, it will travel longer on:

Options: (a) rocky soil (b) marble floor (c) floor of bricks (d) ground

mcqs.q: What is force?
mcqs.why: Force is a push or a pull applied on a body. When we push or pull a body, we apply force on it and the body may start moving, change speed or stop.

mcqs.q: When a body changes its position, it is called:
mcqs.why: When a body changes its position, it is called motion. Force, friction and gravity are forces; the change of position itself is motion.

mcqs.q: All bodies are attracted towards the Earth due to:
mcqs.why: All bodies are attracted towards the Earth due to gravity. The Earth pulls bodies towards itself with this force, which acts on all objects.

mcqs.why: A toy car travels longer where there is less friction. A marble floor is smooth, so it has less friction than rocky soil, a floor of bricks or the ground, and the car travels longer on it.

mcqs.why: A pulley consists of a grooved wheel with a rope passing over it. A lever is a rod, an inclined plane is a ramp, and a gear is a toothed wheel, so the grooved wheel belongs to the pulley.

mcqs.why: Friction is the force that stops or tends to stop moving objects. It occurs when a body moves in contact with another body, and it always acts against the direction of movement.

mcqs.why: Everything that makes our work easier is called a machine. Lever, pulley, gear and ramp (inclined plane) are simple machines that help make motion easier.

mcqs.q: Gravity acts on:
mcqs.why: The Earth pulls bodies towards itself with the force called gravity, and it acts on all objects — for example leaves fall to the ground and a ball thrown upward returns to the ground.

mcqs.q: Friction always acts:
mcqs.why: Friction is the force that stops or tends to stop moving objects, for example a kicked football stops after covering a certain distance. Friction always acts against the direction of movement.

Key Points

  • Force and motion are closely related: force can start a body moving, increase or decrease its speed, change its direction, or stop it.
  • We cannot walk on ice easily because there is very little friction on its smooth surface; friction between the pencil tip and paper makes writing possible.
  • Everything that makes our work easier is called a machine; machines change the amount and direction of force.
  • For an icy surface the ice-skate boot with a blade is suitable; for a playground, a sports shoe with studs; for rocky soil, a strong boot with a thick rough sole.
  • A ramp (inclined plane) helps to take a wheelchair up to a stage because it needs less force to move objects up.
  • While writing we use a push force; pencils become blunt because friction wears the tip down.

Solved Exercises

Q: How force and motion are related? Explain.

Ans: Force and motion are closely related. When we push or pull a body, we apply force on it, and the body starts moving, that is, it changes its position, which is called motion. Force can also increase or decrease the speed of a moving body, change its direction of motion, or stop it.

Q: What is meant by gravity? On which objects it acts?

Ans: The Earth pulls bodies towards itself with a specific force, and this force is called gravity. It acts on all objects — for example, the leaves of a tree fall to the ground, fountain water falls on the ground, and a ball thrown upward returns to the ground after reaching a certain height because of gravity.

Q: Define friction. In which direction it acts?

Ans: Friction is the force that stops or tends to stop moving objects. It occurs when a body moves in contact with another body, for example when a kicked football stops after covering a certain distance. Friction always acts against the direction of movement.

Q: What is a machine and how does it work for us?

Ans: Everything that makes our work easier is called a machine. Machines make our work easier by changing the amount and direction of force, so that heavy things can be lifted with less force. Lever, pulley, gear and ramp (inclined plane) are simple machines that help make motion easier.

Q: Why cannot we walk on ice easily?

Ans: We cannot walk on ice easily because there is very little friction on the smooth surface of ice. The chapter tells us that we cannot walk on Earth without friction, and if there is less friction it becomes difficult to walk. On ice our feet slip instead of gripping the ground, so walking becomes difficult.

Q: Look carefully at the pictures given below. Which one of these shoes is suitable for rocky soil, which one for playground and which one for icy surface? Explain the reason in your answer.

Ans: The shoe for the icy surface is the ice-skate boot with a blade (first picture), because its smooth blade slides easily over ice where there is very little friction. The shoe for the playground is the blue sports shoe with studs (middle picture), because the studs give it a better grip on the ground through friction, so the player does not slip while running. The shoe for rocky soil is the high, strong boot with laces and a thick rough sole (third picture), because it protects the foot on hard, uneven rocky ground and its rough sole provides friction for grip.

Q: The patient is sitting in a wheelchair. Which machine will be helpful to take him on stage and why?

Ans: The ramp (inclined plane) shown in the lower picture will be helpful, not the lever shown in the upper picture. An inclined plane is a simple machine with one end relatively higher than the other, and it requires less force and energy to move objects from one place to another. With a ramp placed against the stage, the wheelchair can be pushed easily from the bottom to the top.

mcqs.why: While writing, we use a push force. We press the pencil against the paper and push it along to form the letters, just as throwing an object is pushing it.

chapters.title: Chapter 7: The Earth and its Resources

lessons.title: Multiple Choice Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Natural resources are the basic materials that humans get from land, sea or air; everything we use is made from natural resources.
  • Renewable resources are unlimited resources which can be replaced after use, for example air, water, soil, forests and solar energy.
  • Non-renewable resources are limited, for example coal, petrol, diesel, natural gas and oil; they take millions of years to form and cannot be replaced easily once used.
  • Fossils are the remains or imprints of organisms that lived on the Earth long ago, found under rocks, soil and under the sea; they give information about extinct animals like dinosaurs.
  • Glass is made from sand. About 29 percent of the Earth's surface is land. About 97 percent of the water on Earth is in the oceans and only 3 percent is freshwater.
  • To make things reusable is called recycling. Deforestation destroys the homes of animals and reduces fresh air.

Solved Exercises

Q: Glass is made from:

Options: (a) sugar. (b) sand. (c) plastic. (d) rubber.

Correct answer: sand.

Q: About what percentage of the Earth's surface is land?

Options: (a) 1 percent (b) 21 percent (c) 29 percent (d) 30 percent

Correct answer: 29 percent

Q: Remains of dead animals and plants found in the earth are called:

Options: (a) soil. (b) minerals. (c) stones. (d) fossils.

Correct answer: fossils.

Q: To make things reusable is called:

Options: (a) recycling. (b) conservation of resources. (c) care. (d) cycling.

Correct answer: recycling.

Q: An example of non-renewable resources is:

Options: (a) oil. (b) soil. (c) air. (d) solar energy.

Correct answer: oil.

mcqs.q: Glass is made from:
mcqs.why: Glass is made from sand. Sand is melted at high temperature to make glass; sugar, plastic and rubber are not used to make glass.

mcqs.q: About what percentage of the Earth's surface is land?
mcqs.why: About 29 percent of the Earth's surface is land. The remaining large part of the Earth's surface is covered with water, mostly in the oceans.

mcqs.q: Remains of dead animals and plants found in the earth are called:
mcqs.why: Remains of dead animals and plants found in the earth are called fossils. They are preserved under rocks, soil and under the sea and tell us about living things of long ago.

mcqs.q: To make things reusable is called:
mcqs.why: To make things reusable is called recycling. Recycling saves natural resources because old things are used again instead of making everything new.

mcqs.q: An example of non-renewable resources is:
mcqs.why: Oil is an example of a non-renewable resource: it is limited, takes millions of years to form and cannot be replaced easily. Soil, air and solar energy are renewable resources.

mcqs.q: Which one of the following is a renewable resource?
mcqs.why: Forests are called renewable resources because they can be replaced after use: new trees can be planted and grown again in place of the trees that are cut. Coal, petrol and natural gas are non-renewable.

mcqs.why: About 97% of the water present on Earth is in the oceans. Only the remaining 3% is present in glaciers, rivers, streams and lakes as freshwater.

options: animals and plants that live today only
organisms that lived a long time ago, such as dinosaurs
mcqs.why: Fossils are the imprints or remains of organisms that lived on the Earth thousands of years ago. They provide information about animals and plants that do not exist now, such as dinosaurs.

mcqs.q: Non-renewable resources take how long to form?
mcqs.why: Non-renewable resources such as coal, petrol, diesel and natural gas take millions of years to form, and once they are used, they cannot be replaced by new ones easily.

mcqs.q: The basic materials that humans get from land, sea or air are called:
mcqs.why: The basic material that humans get from land, sea or air is called natural resources, and we obtain the basic material for making necessary items of life from them. There is no substitute for natural resources.

lessons.title: Short Answers and Constructed Response Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Forests are renewable resources because new trees can be planted and grown again in place of the trees that are cut.
  • Rainwater is added in rivers and streams, and snow melting on mountains also becomes water; this water flows through rivers and streams and finally falls into lakes and oceans.
  • Two disadvantages of deforestation: it destroys the natural habitats (homes) of animals, and it reduces fresh, oxygenated air and timber and helps cause climatic change and pollution.
  • A complete fossil of a jellyfish cannot be obtained easily because it is a soft animal with no hard parts; its soft body decomposes quickly after death.
  • From the teeth and jaws of fossil skulls we know the feed of animals: sharp, pointed teeth show a meat-eating animal, while a beak-like mouth with no sharp teeth shows a plant-eating animal.
  • Water is renewable, yet people face lack of clean drinking water because only 3 percent is freshwater and careless use and pollution spoil it.

Solved Exercises

Q: What are fossils? About which organisms do they provide information?

Ans: Fossils are the imprints or remains of organisms that lived on the Earth thousands of years ago and are now found under rocks, soil and under the sea. They provide information about animals and plants that lived a long time ago and do not exist now, such as dinosaurs, which lived millions of years ago and are now extinct.

Q: Why are forests called renewable resources?

Ans: Forests are called renewable resources because they are unlimited resources that can be replaced after use. New trees can be planted and grown again in place of the trees that are cut, so forests can be obtained again after their use, like air, water, soil and solar energy.

Q: How does water reach oceans and lakes?

Ans: Rainwater is added in rivers and streams, and the snow falling on mountains also melts and becomes water. This water flows through rivers and streams from the mountains and finally falls into the lakes and oceans. About 97% of the water present on Earth is in the oceans.

Q: Describe any two disadvantages of deforestation.

Ans: First, forests are natural habitats for animals, so cutting forests destroys the homes of many animals. Second, forests provide us fresh and oxygenated air and timber, so deforestation reduces fresh air and land resources and helps cause climatic change and pollution.

Q: Differentiate between renewable and non-renewable resources.

Ans: Renewable resources are unlimited resources which can be replaced after use, for example air, water, soil, forests and solar energy. Non-renewable resources are limited resources such as coal, petrol, diesel and natural gas, which take millions of years to form, and once they are used, they cannot be replaced by new ones easily.

Q: We found the skulls of various animals during the excavation. How do we know about their feed?

Ans: The skulls are fossils — remains of animals preserved in soil and rocks, which are dug out during excavation. We know about their feed from the shape of their teeth and jaws: the skull with a beak-like mouth and no sharp teeth (skull 1) belonged to a plant-eating animal, while the skull with sharp, pointed teeth (skull 2) belonged to a meat-eating animal, because sharp teeth are used for tearing flesh and flat teeth or beaks are used for eating plants.

Q: Jellyfish is a soft invertebrate. Can we obtain fossil of jellyfish?

Ans: A complete fossil of a jellyfish cannot be obtained easily because it is a soft animal with no hard parts like bones or skeleton. Its soft body decomposes quickly after death, so no hard remains are preserved in rocks, soil or under the sea. At most, only its imprint could be preserved if it was buried quickly, like a footprint preserved in a hardened mixture.

mcqs.q: Forests are called renewable resources because:
options: new trees can be planted and grown again in place of the trees that are cut
they are found only in cities
mcqs.why: Forests are renewable resources because they are unlimited resources that can be replaced after use. New trees can be planted and grown again in place of the trees that are cut.

mcqs.q: Water reaches oceans and lakes through:
options: rivers and streams flowing from the mountains
mcqs.why: Rainwater is added in rivers and streams, and the snow falling on mountains also melts and becomes water. This water flows through rivers and streams from the mountains and finally falls into the lakes and oceans.

mcqs.q: Which one is a disadvantage of deforestation?
options: It destroys the natural habitats of animals
mcqs.why: Forests are natural habitats for animals, so cutting forests destroys the homes of many animals. Forests also provide fresh and oxygenated air and timber, so deforestation reduces them too.

mcqs.q: A complete fossil of a jellyfish cannot be obtained easily because:
options: jellyfish live in deep water only
it is a soft animal with no hard parts and its body decomposes quickly
mcqs.why: A jellyfish is a soft invertebrate with no hard parts like bones or skeleton. Its soft body decomposes quickly after death, so no hard remains are preserved in rocks, soil or under the sea.

mcqs.q: A fossil skull with sharp, pointed teeth belonged to:
mcqs.why: We know about the feed of fossil animals from the shape of their teeth and jaws: sharp, pointed teeth are used for tearing flesh, so the skull belonged to a meat-eating animal.

mcqs.q: Only what percentage of the Earth's water is freshwater in glaciers, rivers, streams and lakes?
mcqs.why: About 97% of the water on Earth is in the oceans and only the remaining 3% is present in glaciers, rivers, streams and lakes as freshwater, so clean drinking water can become short.

mcqs.q: Which one of the following is made from a natural resource obtained from a tree?
options: A pencil made from the wood of a tree
A glass made from sand only
A brick made from clay only
mcqs.why: Everything we use is made from natural resources in one way or the other, such as a pencil made from the wood of a tree and a rubber obtained from a rubber tree.

mcqs.q: Dinosaurs are animals that:
options: lived millions of years ago and are now extinct
mcqs.why: Fossils provide information about animals and plants that lived a long time ago and do not exist now, such as dinosaurs, which lived millions of years ago and are now extinct.

mcqs.q: If resources are used carelessly by a growing population, then:
options: we will have fewer resources than in the past
new resources will form in days
mcqs.why: The Earth has limited natural resources, and non-renewable resources take millions of years to form. Growing population and lavish use are rapidly reducing them, so we have fewer resources unless we conserve them carefully.

mcqs.q: Which group contains only renewable resources?
options: Air, water, soil, forests and solar energy
mcqs.why: Renewable resources are unlimited resources which can be replaced after use, for example air, water, soil, forests and solar energy. Coal, petrol, diesel and natural gas are non-renewable.
