Q: Is there anything that is not made from natural resources?

Ans: No. The basic material that humans get from land, sea or air is called natural resources, and we obtain the basic material for making necessary items of life from land, sea or air. So everything we use, such as a pencil made from the wood of a tree and a rubber obtained from a rubber tree, is made from natural resources in one way or the other. There is no substitute for natural resources.

Q: Water is a renewable resource. There should be plenty of water for every human being on the Earth but why is it not so?

Ans: Although water is a renewable resource, about 97% of the water on Earth is in the oceans and only the remaining 3% is present in glaciers, rivers, streams and lakes as freshwater. Due to growing population and careless use, humans are facing lack of clean drinking water and water pollution, so if water is not used carefully, even this renewable resource can run out or become unusable.

Q: Is it possible that we have more resources than those of the past?

Ans: No, it is not possible. The Earth has limited natural resources, and non-renewable resources like coal, petrol and natural gas take millions of years to form and cannot be replaced easily once used. Growing population and lavish use of resources are rapidly reducing them, so we have fewer resources than in the past, not more, unless we conserve them carefully.

lessons.title: Multiple Choice Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Weather is the daily condition of the environment or atmosphere of a location; it is a short duration condition. Climate is the general and average weather conditions of an area over a long time.
  • On the basis of climate, the Earth is divided into three zones: Tropical, Temperate and Polar.
  • The Tropical Zone receives vertical Sun rays, so it is hot. The Polar Zone receives the most slanting and weak rays, so its climate is extremely cold.
  • Pakistan is located in the Temperate Zone, where the Sun rays fall slant, so the climate is mild.
  • Due to smoke and gases emitted from factories and vehicles, the average temperature of the Earth is increasing.
  • With the rise of height from sea level, the climate becomes cooler and the winter season becomes longer.

Solved Exercises

Q: If it rains suddenly, what do you observe?

Options: (a) Weather condition (b) Climate (c) Weather and climate (d) Location

Correct answer: Weather condition

Q: Which zone of the Earth receives vertical Sun rays?

Options: (a) Temperate (b) Tropical (c) Polar (d) All of these

Correct answer: Tropical

Q: The climate of the regions of Polar Zone is:

Options: (a) extremely cold. (b) warm. (c) humid. (d) mild.

Correct answer: extremely cold.

Q: Due to the smoke and gases emitted from factories and vehicles, the average temperature of the Earth is:

Options: (a) increasing. (b) decreasing. (c) not affected. (d) sometime increasing and sometime decreasing.

Correct answer: increasing.

Q: In how many zones the Earth is divided on the basis of climate?

Options: (a) 2 (b) 3 (c) 4 (d) 5

Correct answer: 3

mcqs.q: If it rains suddenly, what do you observe?
mcqs.why: Sudden rain is a weather condition. Weather is the daily condition of the atmosphere of a location, which may last one or many days, while climate is the average condition over a long time.

mcqs.q: Which zone of the Earth receives vertical Sun rays?
mcqs.why: The Tropical Zone of the Earth receives vertical Sun rays, so it is the hot zone. The Temperate Zone receives slant rays and the Polar Zone receives the most slanting rays.

mcqs.q: The climate of the regions of Polar Zone is:
mcqs.why: The climate of the regions of the Polar Zone is extremely cold, because here the Sun rays are more slanted and weak and the temperature is minimum at the poles.

mcqs.q: Due to the smoke and gases emitted from factories and vehicles, the average temperature of the Earth is:
mcqs.why: Due to the smoke and gases emitted from factories and vehicles, the average temperature of the Earth is increasing. This is making the climate of the Earth warmer.

mcqs.q: In how many zones the Earth is divided on the basis of climate?
mcqs.why: On the basis of climate, the Earth is divided into 3 zones: the Tropical Zone, the Temperate Zone and the Polar Zone.

mcqs.q: Weather is:
options: the average condition of an area over a long time
the daily condition of the atmosphere of a location
mcqs.why: Weather is the daily condition of the environment or atmosphere of a location. Its duration may be one or many days, so it is a short duration condition.

mcqs.q: Climate is:
options: the general and average weather conditions of an area over a long time
the rain of one season only
mcqs.why: Climate is the general and average weather conditions of an area, which describe the general and long-lasting weather conditions of that area, unlike weather which is for a short duration.

mcqs.q: Pakistan is located in which climate zone?
mcqs.why: Our country Pakistan is located in the Temperate Zone, which is located between the Tropical and Polar Zones. Here the Sun rays fall slant, so the climate is mild.

mcqs.q: The climate of the Temperate Zone is:
mcqs.why: In the Temperate Zone the Sun rays fall slant and are weak, so its climate is mild — neither as hot as the Tropical Zone nor as cold as the Polar Zone.

mcqs.q: With the rise of height from sea level, the climate becomes:
mcqs.why: With the rise of height from the sea level, the climate becomes cooler and the duration of winter season increases. Places at greater height have a cooler climate.

lessons.title: Short Answers and Constructed Response Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Near the equator the Sun rays fall vertically, so the climate is hot; as we move away from the equator the rays become more slant and weak and the climate becomes less hot, with minimum temperature at the poles.
  • Skardu is at a great height from sea level, so its temperature falls below zero in winter; Karachi is near the sea at low height, so its winter temperature remains mild.
  • On the figure of the Earth, the bands from top to bottom are: Polar Zone, Temperate Zone, Tropical Zone (around the Equator), Temperate Zone and Polar Zone.
  • The Moon has no air, clouds or water like the Earth, so there are no storms, rains and snowfall on the Moon and it has no weather like ours.
  • A wind vane shows the direction from which the wind is blowing; a rain gauge measures the amount of rain, read on a millimetre scale.

Solved Exercises

Q: Differentiate between weather and climate.

Ans: Weather is the daily condition of the environment or atmosphere of a location. Its duration may be one or many days, so it is a short duration condition. Climate is the general and average weather conditions of an area, which describe the general and long-lasting weather conditions of that area.

Q: What is the relation between climate and the height from sea level?

Ans: With the rise of height from the sea level, the climate becomes cooler and the duration of winter season increases. So places at greater height from sea level have a cooler climate, while places near sea level have a milder climate.

Q: Why does climate change with distance from the equator?

Ans: The climate or weather changes of any region depend upon falling of Sun rays vertically or slanting. Near the equator the Sun rays fall vertically, so the climate there is hot. As we move away from the equator, the Sun rays become more slant and weak and the climate becomes less hot, and eventually the temperature is minimum at the poles.

Q: Why is the climate of Polar Zone very cold?

Ans: The Polar Zone consists of the areas around the north and south poles of the Earth. Here, the Sun rays are more slanted and weak. Therefore, the climate of this zone is the coldest, and the temperature is minimum at the poles.

Q: In which zone, our country is located on the basis of climate? Explain.

Ans: Our country Pakistan is located in the Temperate Zone, which is located between the Tropical and Polar Zones. Here, the Sun rays fall slant, so the climate of this zone is mild due to weak Sun rays, and it is neither as hot as the Tropical Zone nor as cold as the Polar Zone.

Q: Identify the different zones on the figure of the Earth, on the basis of climate.

Ans: Diagram (in words): The figure shows the Earth as a circle divided into horizontal bands by the climate zones, with a thick black line across the middle for the Equator. From top to bottom the bands are: Polar Zone (dark band at the top), Temperate Zone (light pink band), Tropical Zone (narrow dark red band across the centre, around the Equator), Temperate Zone (light pink band) and Polar Zone (dark band at the bottom). The book's labelled diagram on printed page 96 names every label as: Polar Zone, Temperate Zone, Tropical Zone, Equator, Temperate Zone and Polar Zone.

Q: What is the climate of these zones? Describe the reasons.

Ans: The Tropical Zone, around the equator, is hot because here the Sun rays fall vertically. The Temperate Zone, between the Tropical and Polar Zones, has a mild climate because here the Sun rays fall slant and are weak. The Polar Zone, around the north and south poles, is the coldest because here the Sun rays are more slanted and weak.

Q: In winter, the temperature of Skardu, a city of Gilgit Baltistan is below zero degree centigrade while the temperature of Karachi is mild. Why is it so?

Ans: Skardu is a hilly area at a great height from sea level, and with the rise of height from the sea level, the climate becomes cooler and the duration of winter increases, so its temperature falls below zero degree centigrade in winter. Karachi is located near the sea at low height, and waterbodies make the climate of the adjacent land areas mild, so the temperature of Karachi remains mild in winter.

mcqs.q: Near the equator, the climate is hot because:
options: the Sun rays fall slanting there
the Sun rays fall vertically there
mcqs.why: The climate changes of any region depend upon falling of Sun rays vertically or slanting. Near the equator the Sun rays fall vertically, so the climate there is hot.

mcqs.q: The temperature is minimum at the poles because:
options: the Sun rays are vertical there
the Sun rays are the most slant and weak there
the wind does not blow there
mcqs.why: As we move away from the equator, the Sun rays become more slant and weak and the climate becomes less hot, and eventually the temperature is minimum at the poles.

mcqs.q: In winter, the temperature of Skardu falls below zero degree centigrade because Skardu:
options: is a hilly area at a great height from sea level
mcqs.why: Skardu is a hilly area at a great height from sea level, and with the rise of height the climate becomes cooler and the duration of winter increases, so its temperature falls below zero in winter.

mcqs.q: The temperature of Karachi remains mild in winter because Karachi:
options: is located near the sea at low height
mcqs.why: Karachi is located near the sea at low height, and waterbodies make the climate of the adjacent land areas mild, so the temperature of Karachi remains mild in winter.

mcqs.q: In the figure of the Earth, the zone around the Equator is the:
mcqs.why: The bands on the figure from top to bottom are: Polar Zone, Temperate Zone, Tropical Zone across the centre around the Equator, Temperate Zone and Polar Zone.

mcqs.q: The Tropical Zone is hot because in this zone:
mcqs.why: The Tropical Zone, around the equator, is hot because here the Sun rays fall vertically. The Temperate Zone has a mild climate and the Polar Zone is the coldest.

mcqs.q: The Moon has no storms, rains and snowfall because it has:
options: no air, clouds or water like the Earth
mcqs.why: Weather is described in terms of temperature, humidity, precipitation, clouds and winds, and these need air and water. The Moon has no air, clouds or water like the Earth, so there are no storms, rains and snowfall on the Moon.

mcqs.q: A simple wind vane is used to show:
options: the direction from which the wind is blowing
mcqs.why: The arrow of the wind vane turns and points in the direction from which the wind is blowing, so the vane shows the direction of the wind.

mcqs.q: A rain gauge measures the amount of rain on a scale marked in:
mcqs.why: In a simple rain gauge, a paper strip marked in millimetre scale is fixed on a transparent bottle. The level of rainwater collected, read on the millimetre scale, shows the amount of rain.

mcqs.q: Places near sea level have a climate that is:
mcqs.why: With the rise of height from sea level the climate becomes cooler, while places near sea level have a milder climate. Karachi near the sea is an example.

Q: How many weathers are there on the Moon? Does the Moon also have storms, rains and snowfall like our Earth? What is your opinion about the climate of the Moon?

Ans: The Moon has no weather like our Earth. Weather is described in terms of temperature, humidity in air, precipitation (rain or snow), clouds and winds, and these need air and water. The Moon has no air, clouds or water like the Earth, so there are no storms, rains and snowfall on the Moon. In my opinion, the Moon has no climate like the Earth's climate, because its conditions do not change like the daily weather of a place on Earth.

Q: Project: Construct a simple wind vane — what is made and what is observed?

Ans: A simple wind vane is constructed by using cardboard or old carton, scissors, straw, board pins and coloured chart paper according to the diagram. The arrow of the vane is fixed so that it can turn freely on the pin, and it is placed in an open place. It is observed that the arrow turns and points in the direction from which the wind is blowing, so the vane shows the direction of the wind.

Q: Project: Make a simple rain gauge — what is made and what is observed?

Ans: A simple rain gauge is made by using a transparent plastic bottle, scissors, sellotape and a paper strip marked in millimetre scale. The bottle is cut and the marked strip is fixed on it, and the gauge is placed in the open during the rainy season. It is observed and compared that the level of rainwater collected in the gauge, read on the millimetre scale, shows the amount of rain during three days in a rainy season, and the days with more rain show a higher level.

chapters.title: Chapter 9: Earth in the Solar System

lessons.title: Multiple Choice Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • The eight planets in order from the Sun are: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. Saturn is the planet with rings.
  • The gravity of the Sun keeps the planets and other celestial bodies together in the Solar System.
  • The Earth completes its revolution around the Sun in 365 days; this period is called a solar year. The Moon completes one revolution around the Earth in 29.5 days.
  • Seasons change due to the annual revolution of the Earth and the tilt of its axis. When it is winter in the northern hemisphere, it is summer in the southern hemisphere.
  • Pakistan is situated in the northern hemisphere. Venus is the planet that does not have any Moon.
  • In a solar eclipse the Moon comes between the Sun and the Earth; in a lunar eclipse the Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon. A solar eclipse is usually partial because the Moon is much smaller than the Earth.

Solved Exercises

Q: The gravity of which body keeps the planets and other celestial bodies together in the Solar System?

Options: (a) Jupiter (b) Earth (c) Sun (d) Moon

Correct answer: Sun

Q: The Earth completes its rotation around the Sun in 365 days. This period is called:

Options: (a) solar year. (b) solar month. (c) lunar month. (d) lunar year.

Correct answer: solar year.

Q: Due to the annual revolution of Earth and tilt of its axis:

Options: (a) day and night are formed. (b) seasons change. (c) eclipses are formed. (d) shadows are formed.

Correct answer: seasons change.

Q: On the globe, in which part of the Earth is Pakistan situated?

Options: (a) Northern hemisphere (b) Southern hemisphere (c) Equator (d) Half in northern and half in southern hemisphere

Correct answer: Northern hemisphere

Q: Which planet of the Solar System does not have any Moon?

Options: (a) Jupiter (b) Venus (c) Mars (d) Saturn

Correct answer: Venus

mcqs.q: The gravity of which body keeps the planets and other celestial bodies together in the Solar System?
mcqs.why: The gravity of the Sun keeps the planets and other celestial bodies together in the Solar System. All the planets keep revolving around the Sun due to its gravity.

mcqs.q: The Earth completes its rotation around the Sun in 365 days. This period is called:
mcqs.why: Going around the Sun is the Earth's revolution (orbital movement). The Earth completes its one revolution around the Sun in 365 days, and this period is called a solar year. (The book's stem says 'rotation'; the movement around the Sun is revolution.)

mcqs.q: Due to the annual revolution of Earth and tilt of its axis:
mcqs.why: Seasons change due to the annual revolution of the Earth and the tilt of its axis. Day and night are formed by the rotation of the Earth, not by its revolution.

mcqs.q: On the globe, in which part of the Earth is Pakistan situated?
options: Half in northern and half in southern hemisphere
mcqs.why: On the globe, Pakistan is situated in the northern hemisphere, the half of the Earth that is north of the Equator.

mcqs.q: Which planet of the Solar System does not have any Moon?
mcqs.why: Venus does not have any Moon. Jupiter, Mars and Saturn all have moons, but Venus has none.

mcqs.q: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
mcqs.why: Mercury is the planet closest to the Sun. It is the first planet of the Solar System and revolves closest to the Sun, at a distance of about 50 million kilometres from the Sun.

mcqs.q: In how many days does the Moon complete one revolution around the Earth?
mcqs.why: The Moon completes its one revolution around the Earth in 29.5 days, while the Earth completes its one revolution around the Sun in 365 days.

mcqs.q: The planet with rings around it is:
mcqs.why: In the picture of the Solar System, the planets in order are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, and Saturn is the planet with rings.

mcqs.q: When it is winter in the northern hemisphere, the season in the southern hemisphere is:
mcqs.why: When it is winter in the northern hemisphere, it is summer in the southern hemisphere, because the southern hemisphere then receives more direct rays and has longer days.

mcqs.q: A solar eclipse is usually partial because:
options: the Moon is much smaller than the Earth, so its shadow falls only on a small part of the Earth
mcqs.why: The complete solar eclipse is very rare and usually we see partial solar eclipses, because the Moon is much smaller than the Earth, so its shadow falls only on a small part of the Earth.

lessons.title: Short Answers and Constructed Response Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • We see only one side of the Moon because the Moon completes one rotation about its own axis in the same time in which it completes one trip around the Earth.
  • If there were no tilt in the Earth's axis, the seasons would not change and the same season would remain all the year.
  • Mercury is the planet closest to the Sun, at a distance of about 50 million kilometres from the Sun.
  • The movement of a body around another body is its orbital movement (revolution); the movement on its own axis is its axial movement (rotation).
  • In the southern hemisphere the seasons are opposite to the northern hemisphere: 21 March — Autumn, 22 June — Winter, 23 September — Spring, 22 December — Summer.
  • The Sun is the biggest source of light and heat for the Earth; without it the Earth would become dark and very cold and life would not be possible.

Solved Exercises

Q: We can only see one side of the Moon. Explain.

Ans: The Moon also rotates about its own axis. In the same duration in which it completes one trip around the Earth, it also completes one rotation about its own axis. That is why we can see only the same one half of the surface of the Moon, and we never see the other half.

Q: If there were no tilt in the Earth's axis, how would have it affected the seasons?

Ans: Seasons change because of the annual revolution of the Earth and the tilt of its axis. If there were no tilt in the Earth's axis, the Sun rays would not fall vertically on one hemisphere and slanting on the other at different times of the year. So day and night would stay equal and the seasons would not change; the same season would remain all the year.

Q: When it is winter in the northern hemisphere then what will be the season in southern hemisphere?

Ans: When it is winter in the northern hemisphere, it is summer in the southern hemisphere. At that time the northern hemisphere receives slanting Sun rays, so its days are shorter, while the southern hemisphere receives more direct rays and has longer days.

Q: Which planet is closest to the Sun?

Ans: Mercury is the planet closest to the Sun. It is the first planet of the Solar System and revolves closest to the Sun, at a distance of about 50 million kilometres from the Sun.

Q: Why is the solar eclipse usually partial?

Ans: The complete solar eclipse is very rare and usually we see partial solar eclipses. It is because the Moon is much smaller than the Earth, so its shadow falls only on a small part of the Earth. Therefore, the solar eclipse can be seen only in those parts of the Earth.

Q: Which phenomena are shown in the following figure?

Ans: Diagram (in words): The figure has two diagrams, each labelled Sun, Moon and Earth, with dotted circles showing the orbit of the Earth around the Sun and the orbit of the Moon around the Earth. In the left diagram the Moon is between the Sun and the Earth, so the Moon's shadow falls on the Earth — this is a solar eclipse. In the right diagram the Earth is between the Sun and the Moon, so the Earth's shadow falls on the Moon — this is a lunar eclipse.

Q: In the following picture, each arrowhead shows the axial or orbital movement of Earth and Moon. Write the correct type of movement in the box given near each arrowhead.

Ans: Diagram (in words): The picture shows the Sun in the centre-right, the Earth on its large dotted orbit around the Sun, and the Moon on its small dotted orbit around the Earth, with five empty boxes near the arrowheads. The arrow going around the Sun itself shows the axial movement (rotation) of the Sun. The big blue arrowhead on the Earth's orbit around the Sun shows the orbital movement (revolution) of the Earth. The small curved arrow on the Earth shows the axial movement (rotation) of the Earth. The arrowhead on the Moon's orbit around the Earth shows the orbital movement (revolution) of the Moon. The small curved arrow on the Moon shows the axial movement (rotation) of the Moon.

Q: In how many days, the Moon completes its one revolution around the Earth? _____

Ans: 29.5 days

Q: In how many days, the Earth completes its one revolution around the Sun? _____

Ans: 365 days

Q: Identify the season in the southern hemisphere as per given figure. Write the correct season in the boxes given near the dates.

Ans: Diagram (in words): The figure shows the Sun in the centre and the Earth at four positions around it, labelled 21 March, 22 June (with labels Axis, Equator and Earth), 23 September and 22 December, with pink arrows showing the direction of revolution. The seasons in the southern hemisphere are opposite to the northern hemisphere: 21 March — Autumn (equal day and night); 22 June — Winter (the southern hemisphere receives slanting rays, so its day is shortest); 23 September — Spring (equal day and night); 22 December — Summer (the southern hemisphere receives vertical rays, so its day is longest).

Q: Write the names of the planets in this picture.

Ans: Diagram (in words): The picture shows the Sun on the left and eight planets in a row, numbered 1 to 8 in order of distance from the Sun. 1 — Mercury, 2 — Venus, 3 — Earth, 4 — Mars, 5 — Jupiter, 6 — Saturn (the planet with rings), 7 — Uranus, 8 — Neptune.

mcqs.q: We can see only one side of the Moon because:
options: the Moon does not rotate at all
the Moon completes one rotation about its axis in the same time as one trip around the Earth
the other side is always dark with no surface
the Earth blocks the other side
mcqs.why: The Moon also rotates about its own axis. In the same duration in which it completes one trip around the Earth, it also completes one rotation about its own axis, so we see only the same one half of its surface.

mcqs.q: If there were no tilt in the Earth's axis, then:
options: the seasons would not change and the same season would remain all the year
mcqs.why: Seasons change because of the annual revolution of the Earth and the tilt of its axis. Without the tilt, day and night would stay equal and the seasons would not change.

mcqs.q: In a lunar eclipse:
options: the Moon comes between the Sun and the Earth
the Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon
the Sun comes between the Earth and the Moon
mcqs.why: In a lunar eclipse the Earth is between the Sun and the Moon, so the Earth's shadow falls on the Moon. In a solar eclipse the Moon is between the Sun and the Earth.

mcqs.q: In a solar eclipse:
options: the Moon comes between the Sun and the Earth
the Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon
the Moon's shadow falls on the Sun
the Sun hides behind the Earth
mcqs.why: In a solar eclipse the Moon is between the Sun and the Earth, so the Moon's shadow falls on the Earth and the Sun is hidden for those parts of the Earth.

mcqs.q: The movement of the Earth around the Sun is called its:
mcqs.why: The arrow going along the Earth's orbit around the Sun shows its orbital movement (revolution), while the small curved arrow on the Earth itself shows its axial movement (rotation).

mcqs.q: On 22 December, the season in the southern hemisphere is:
mcqs.why: The seasons in the southern hemisphere are opposite to the northern hemisphere. On 22 December the southern hemisphere receives vertical rays and its day is longest, so it is Summer there.

mcqs.q: On 22 June, the season in the southern hemisphere is:
mcqs.why: On 22 June the southern hemisphere receives slanting rays and its day is shortest, so it is Winter in the southern hemisphere, while the northern hemisphere has summer.

mcqs.q: If the Sun stops providing light and heat, then:
options: the Earth will become dark and very cold and life will not be possible
mcqs.why: The Sun is the biggest source of light and heat for our Earth, and life on the Earth exists due to the Sun. Without it, plants will not grow, day and seasons will end, and living things will not survive.

mcqs.q: Mercury is at a distance of about how much from the Sun?
mcqs.why: Mercury is the planet closest to the Sun. It is the first planet of the Solar System and revolves closest to the Sun, at a distance of about 50 million kilometres from the Sun.

mcqs.q: The eighth and last planet in order from the Sun is:
mcqs.why: The eight planets in order of distance from the Sun are: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. So Neptune is the eighth and last planet.

Q: If the Sun stops providing light and heat, what will be its effects on the Earth? Would life be possible on the Earth?

Ans: The Sun is the biggest source of light and heat for our Earth, and life on the Earth exists due to the Sun. If the Sun stops providing light and heat, the Earth will become dark and very cold. Plants will not grow, day and seasons will end, and living things will not survive. So life would not be possible on the Earth without the Sun.

Q: Project: Models of lunar eclipse and solar eclipse — what is made and what is observed?

Ans: Make two groups in the class. One group makes the model of lunar eclipse (as in Activity 9.5: a torch as the Sun, a football as the Earth and a tennis ball as the Moon placed in one line, so the shadow of the football falls on the tennis ball) and the other group makes the model of solar eclipse (as in Activity 9.6: the tennis ball as the Moon is placed nearer to the football as the Earth, so the shadow of the tennis ball falls on only some part of the football). It is observed that in a lunar eclipse the Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon and the Moon looks dark, while in a solar eclipse the Moon comes between the Sun and the Earth and the Sun is hidden; the solar eclipse is usually partial because the Moon's shadow covers only a small part of the Earth.

lessons.title: Multiple Choice Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A clinical thermometer is used to check fever. Before using it, it is given a few jerks to bring the mercury or alcohol level down into the bulb.
  • An instant cold pack is used to reduce inflammation as a first aid. The blood pressure 160/100 is high blood pressure.
  • Taking photographs of oneself is known as a selfie.
  • A cube has 6 surfaces, 8 corners and 12 edges. A prism (with triangular ends) has 6 corners, 9 edges and 5 surfaces. A cone has 1 corner, 1 edge and 2 surfaces. A sphere has 1 surface and no corners or edges.
  • A cone has a flat circular base and its sides slope up to one pointed top (apex); a prism has two same-shaped flat ends joined by flat rectangular sides.
  • Models are made from kneaded clay, because ordinary soil is dry and loose, does not bind together and cannot hold a shape.

Solved Exercises

Q: Clinical thermometer is used to:

Options: (a) make shapes (b) measure inflamation in the body (c) check fever (d) measure blood pressure

Correct answer: check fever

Q: The number of corners of a prism are:

Options: (a) 3 (b) 4 (c) 5 (d) 6

Correct answer: 6

Q: The surfaces of a cube are:

Options: (a) 3 (b) 4 (c) 6 (d) 8

Correct answer: 6

Q: Taking photographs of oneself is known as:

Options: (a) portrait (b) selfie (c) landscape (d) oneself

Correct answer: selfie

Q: Which item is used to reduce inflamation as a first aid?

Options: (a) medical tape (b) tweezer (c) thermometer (d) instant cold pack

Correct answer: instant cold pack

Q: The blood pressure 160/100 is:

Options: (a) low blood pressure (b) high blood pressure (c) normal blood pressure (d) not possible

Correct answer: high blood pressure

mcqs.q: Clinical thermometer is used to:
mcqs.why: A clinical thermometer is used to check fever, that is, to measure the temperature of the body when a person is ill. It is not used to make shapes or to measure blood pressure.

mcqs.q: The number of corners of a prism are:
mcqs.why: A prism with triangular ends has 6 corners: three corners at one triangular end and three at the other end. So the number of corners of a prism is 6.

mcqs.q: The surfaces of a cube are:
mcqs.why: A cube has 6 surfaces (faces): top, bottom and four sides. So the surfaces of a cube are 6.

mcqs.q: Taking photographs of oneself is known as:
mcqs.why: Taking photographs of oneself is known as a selfie. A portrait is a photograph of a person taken by someone else, and a landscape shows scenery.

mcqs.q: Which item is used to reduce inflamation as a first aid?
mcqs.why: As a first aid, an instant cold pack is used to reduce inflammation. Medical tape, tweezers and a thermometer do not reduce inflammation.

mcqs.q: The blood pressure 160/100 is:
mcqs.why: The blood pressure 160/100 is higher than the normal blood pressure, so it is high blood pressure. It is neither low nor normal.

mcqs.q: Before using a clinical thermometer, it is given a few jerks to:
options: bring the mercury or alcohol level down into the bulb
mcqs.why: A clinical thermometer is given a few jerks to bring the mercury or alcohol level down into the bulb, so that it starts from a low level and gives the correct body temperature reading.

mcqs.q: The number of corners of a cube is:
mcqs.why: A cube has 8 corners, 12 edges and 6 surfaces. The corners are the points where its edges meet: four at the top and four at the bottom.

mcqs.q: A cone has a flat circular base and its sides slope up to:
mcqs.why: A cone has a flat circular base and its sides slope up to one pointed top (apex), like the cone model shown in the chapter. A prism, on the other hand, has two same-shaped flat ends and no pointed top.

mcqs.q: Models are made from kneaded clay and not from any ordinary soil because ordinary soil:
options: is dry and loose and cannot hold a shape
mcqs.why: Ordinary soil of any kind is dry and loose, does not bind together and cannot hold a shape. So only suitable clay, kneaded by mixing a little water and stretching and compressing it, or play dough can be used to make models.

lessons.title: Short Answers and Constructed Response Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A paper cutter cuts folded paper in one straight, clean cut along the fold, so it is better than scissors for folded paper; before cutting with scissors, a line is drawn first so that the paper is cut straight and in the correct shape.
  • An envelope can be made from a square-shaped paper by folding its corners to the centre and gluing the edges.
  • Everyday items: circle — a coin and a clock face; cube — a dice and an ice cube; cylinder — a water bottle and a gas cylinder; cone — an ice-cream cone and a traffic cone; prism — a tent and a Toblerone chocolate box.
  • A circle cut into 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 equal parts gives each part as 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/5 and 1/6 of the total.
  • A mobile phone is not only used to make a call; it is also a clock, a calendar, a camera and a calculator, so its technology is progressing rapidly.

Solved Exercises

Q: What is the difference between a cone and a prism?

Ans: A cone has a flat circular base and its sides slope up to one pointed top (apex), like the cone model shown in the chapter. A prism has two same-shaped flat ends (in the chapter's model, triangular ends) joined by flat rectangular sides, and it has no pointed top. So a cone has a round base and a point, while a prism has flat faces with two matching ends.

Q: Can an envelope be made from a square shape paper? Explain.

Ans: Yes, an envelope can be made from a square-shaped paper, as shown in Activity 10.6. Fold the paper vertically in half, open it, fold it horizontally in half and open it again, then place it with its corners on the vertical and horizontal lines. Fold the left and right corners to meet at the centre, fold the bottom corner up a little above the centre and glue its edges, and fold the top corner down to make the flap of the envelope.

Q: Why a line is drawn on a paper before cutting it with a scissors?

Ans: Paper and cardboard can be cut with the help of scissors. It is better to draw a line first and then cut along the line carefully, because the line guides us so that the paper is cut straight and in the correct shape.

Q: Why a clinical thermometer is given jerks for a few times before using it?

Ans: A clinical thermometer is given a few jerks to bring the mercury or alcohol level down into the bulb, as told in Activity 10.15. This is done so that the thermometer starts from a low level and gives the correct body temperature reading. It is not needed for a digital thermometer.

Q: Why any soil cannot be used to make a model?

Ans: Models are made from kneaded clay, which is prepared by mixing a little water in clay and stretching and compressing it many times like flour dough (Activity 10.9). Ordinary soil of any kind is dry and loose, does not bind together and cannot hold a shape. So only suitable clay, kneaded in this way, or play dough can be used to make models.

Q: A circular shape is cut as shown in the following figure. What is the value in fraction of the total in each case? Write below each shape.

Ans: Diagram (in words): The figure shows five circles, each cut into equal parts with one part separated. From left to right: the first (blue) circle is cut into 2 equal parts, so each part is 1/2 of the total; the second (orange) circle is cut into 3 equal parts, so each part is 1/3; the third (green) circle is cut into 4 equal parts, so each part is 1/4; the fourth (yellow-green) circle is cut into 5 equal parts (4 in place and 1 separated below), so each part is 1/5; the fifth (purple) circle is cut into 6 equal parts (5 in place and 1 separated), so each part is 1/6.

Q: Identify the various items used in everyday life which look like a circle, a cube, a cylinder, a cone and a prism. Give two examples of each shape.

Ans: Circle: a coin and a clock face (or a plate). Cube: a dice and an ice cube (or a sugar cube). Cylinder: a water bottle and a gas cylinder (or a pipe). Cone: an ice-cream cone and a traffic cone (or a funnel). Prism: a tent and a Toblerone chocolate box (or a roof-shaped prism). These are the same kinds of shapes — sphere, cube, prism, cylinder and cone — whose models are made with clay or play dough in this chapter.

Q: Write below each shape, number of its corners, edges and surfaces.

Ans: Diagram (in words): The figure shows five shapes in a row — a sphere (blue ball), a cube (orange), a pyramid (green), a cone (pink) and a prism (brown, with a triangular end) — with blank lines below for Corners, Edges and Surfaces. Sphere: corners 0, edges 0, surfaces 1. Cube: corners 8, edges 12, surfaces 6. Pyramid: corners 4, edges 6, surfaces 4. Cone: corners 1, edges 1, surfaces 2. Prism: corners 6, edges 9, surfaces 5.

Q: Why is use of paper cutter better than the scissors?

Ans: Paper can be cut easily by using a paper cutter or a knife: the paper is folded along the line, the blade of the paper knife is inserted inside the fold and pushed forward, which cuts the folded paper in one straight, clean cut along the fold. Scissors need the line to be drawn first and the cutting done carefully bit by bit, so the cutter gives a quicker and straighter cut on folded paper.

mcqs.q: A paper cutter is better than scissors for cutting folded paper because it:
options: cuts the paper in one straight, clean cut along the fold
mcqs.why: The paper is folded along the line and the blade of the paper knife is pushed forward inside the fold, which cuts the folded paper in one straight, clean cut. Scissors need the line drawn first and cutting done carefully bit by bit.

mcqs.q: Before cutting paper with scissors, a line is drawn on the paper so that:
options: the paper is cut straight and in the correct shape
mcqs.why: It is better to draw a line first and then cut along the line carefully, because the line guides us so that the paper is cut straight and in the correct shape.

mcqs.q: An envelope can be made from which shaped paper?
mcqs.why: Yes, an envelope can be made from a square-shaped paper: fold the left and right corners to meet at the centre, fold the bottom corner up and glue its edges, and fold the top corner down to make the flap.

mcqs.q: Which pair of everyday items look like a cylinder?
options: A coin and a clock face
A water bottle and a gas cylinder
A dice and an ice cube
An ice-cream cone and a traffic cone
mcqs.why: A water bottle and a gas cylinder (or a pipe) look like a cylinder. A coin is a circle shape, a dice is a cube, and an ice-cream cone is a cone shape.

mcqs.q: A circle is cut into 4 equal parts. Each part is what fraction of the total?
mcqs.why: When a circle is cut into 4 equal parts, each part is 1/4 of the total. In the same way, 2 parts give 1/2, 3 parts give 1/3, 5 parts give 1/5 and 6 parts give 1/6.

mcqs.q: The number of edges of a cube is:
mcqs.why: A cube has 8 corners, 12 edges and 6 surfaces. The 12 edges are the lines where its 6 square surfaces meet.

mcqs.q: A sphere has:
mcqs.why: A sphere, like a ball, is fully round: it has 0 corners, 0 edges and 1 curved surface. A cone has 1 corner, 1 edge and 2 surfaces, and a prism has 6 corners, 9 edges and 5 surfaces.

mcqs.q: A pyramid has how many surfaces?
mcqs.why: In the figure of shapes, the pyramid has 4 corners, 6 edges and 4 surfaces: one base and three triangular sides meeting at the top.

mcqs.q: Mobile phone technology is progressing rapidly because:
options: people want to do more and more tasks quickly with one small device
people make only calls on phones
mcqs.why: A mobile phone is not only used to make a call; it is also a clock, a calendar, a camera and a calculator, and its many Apps are very helpful. Because people need to do more and more tasks quickly with one small device, mobile phone technology is progressing rapidly.

mcqs.q: Which two items look like a cone?
options: An ice-cream cone and a traffic cone

Q: Why mobile phone technology is progressing rapidly? How will be the mobile phone of the future?

Ans: We are living in an information age and we remain in touch with our dears with the help of computer and mobile phone. A mobile phone is not only used to make a call; it is also a clock, a calendar, a camera and a calculator, and its many Apps are very helpful to us. Because people need to do more and more tasks quickly with one small device, mobile phone technology is progressing rapidly. The mobile phone of the future will be even smarter and faster, with more helpful Apps, a better camera and more uses in everyday life.

Q: Project: Making a Nest — what is made and what is observed?

Ans: A bird's nest is made from an empty pack of juice or milk, cotton or cloth and various items for decoration. Steps: (1) Cut the empty pack side for entering and leaving the birds, as shown in the figure. (2) Make it comfortable using cotton and cloths. (3) Make a hole and insert a wire through the upper edge so that it can be hanged on a tree. (4) Use colour ribbon and cardboard to make it fancy. (5) Hang it somewhere near your home or school so that birds can use it. Observation: observe if the birds use it as their nest or not.
